
Using Postgre SQL, I created a database named "DataScienceSkills" for this project.  The password is CC624131 (FOR NOW)
For this project, the original data set, "gsearch.com" was found at Kaggle.com (enter link here). I was unable to load it from the shared GitHub respositry into Postgre SQL so loaded directly from my local drive. 

````{r}
# Connect PostgresSQL database to R to upload my "Movies" database.

DataScienceSkills = dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(),
       dbname='DataScienceSkills',
       host= Sys.getenv("local"),
       port=5432,
       user='postgres',
       password=rstudioapi::askForPassword("Enter password"))

````
  
Let's look at the original file

````{r}

orig_jobsearch <- as_tibble(dbGetQuery(DataScienceSkills, "SELECT * FROM gsearch_jobs"))

head (orig_jobsearch)
````

This original gsearch_jobs file contains 1,820 rows and 26 columns.  Using Postgre SQL, we created five (5) new records, each isolating related variables(columns) while maintaining all 1,820 rows(observations) in each that we will for this analysis. The five tables are "jobs", "job_skills", "job_links", "job_extensions"and  "salary"

Let's look closer at these tables and load them into our environment

````{r jobs}
# load each table into a tibble using dbGetQuery()

jobs <- as_tibble(dbGetQuery(DataScienceSkills, "SELECT * FROM jobs"))
head(jobs)
str(jobs)

job_skills <- as_tibble(dbGetQuery(DataScienceSkills, "SELECT * FROM job_skills"))
head(job_skills)
str(job_skills)

job_links <- as_tibble(dbGetQuery(DataScienceSkills, "SELECT * FROM job_links"))
head(job_links)
str(job_links)

job_extensions <- as_tibble(dbGetQuery(DataScienceSkills, "SELECT * FROM job_extensions"))
head(job_extensions)
str(job_extensions)


salary <- as_tibble(dbGetQuery(DataScienceSkills, "SELECT * FROM salary "))
head(salary)
str(salary)

````
